description: We are an engineering team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge Meknès. Our goal is to develop an innovative solution focused on lunar exploration, landing navigation, and space mission design.
summary: Our project, Lunar Landing Site Navigator, is a 3D computer simulator for autonomous lunar landing powered by Artificial Intelligence and physics-based Guidance, Navigation, and Control (GNC). Designed to address the high-risk challenge of Moon landings—where low lunar gravity ($1.62\text{ m/s}^2$) and zero atmospheric drag require real-time execution—our solution automates vertical/horizontal speed, orientation, and engine thrust control. The system integrates a PPO Reinforcement Learning agent (49/50 success rate in baseline tests), a robust GNC guidance engine (30/30 random start success rate with 45 unit tests passed), a FastAPI WebSocket backend streaming real-time physics at 60 FPS, and a WebGL/Three.js interactive 3D HUD interface. Utilizing NASA LRO/LOLA altimetry, elevation maps, and surface imagery (targeting Shackleton crater at the South Pole), it provides a safe, precise landing platform.
details:
Problem: Landing on the Moon is incredibly difficult due to $1.62\text{ m/s}^2$ lunar gravity and the absence of atmospheric drag. Landers must simultaneously adjust vertical and horizontal velocities, altitude, engine thrust, vector tilting (up to $20^\circ$), and fuel consumption without human intervention.

Our Solution Architecture:

  1. AI Autopilot (PPO Agent): Built using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) reinforcement learning. The agent optimizes thrust and vector control across thousands of simulated descent cycles, achieving 49/50 successful soft landings.
  2. GNC & Physics Engine: Guidance, Navigation, and Control system that models position, velocity, altitude, and fuel burn. Initiated from $1,450\text{ m}$ elevation, it achieves touchdown speeds at $\sim 0.65\text{ m/s}$, passing $30/30$ randomized descent scenarios and 45 automated unit tests.
  3. Real-time 3D Interface & Backend: High-performance FastAPI backend broadcasting WebSocket telemetry 60 times per second to a React + Three.js 3D Aerospace HUD dashboard. Features 3D lander visualization, engine nozzle gimbals, exhaust dust particle effects, pitch/altitude radars, manual override, disturbance testing, and local offline physics fallback.
